details:
Q1: Which log reason should the new "an open base-keyed triage issue already exists" skip use? `skip reason=base_failure_tracked` already exists at `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1681` with `heal_issue=…`. It is paired with the `base_failure_tracked=<n>` GitHub output that drives the note step.
Choices:
A) Use a new, separate reason, for example `skip reason=base_triage_tracked base=<BASE_REF> issue=<N> pr=<PR> check=<check>`. It never writes the `base_failure_tracked` output, so the existing heal-issue key and note step keep their current meaning (RECOMMENDED)
B) Reuse `reason=base_failure_tracked` with `issue=<N>` exactly as the issue says, log only, without writing the `base_failure_tracked` GitHub output. Log parsers then have to tell the two cases apart by `issue=` versus `heal_issue=`
C) Reuse `reason=base_failure_tracked` and also write the `base_failure_tracked=<N>` output, so the note step adds the PR to the base-keyed triage issue the same way it does for heal issues
Q2: How should base-keying fit with the existing heal-issue skip (`TRIAGE_BASE_TRACKED_SKIP_ENABLED`, lines 1637–1698), especially when its job comparison finds `failed_jobs_differ`, meaning the PR fails jobs that main does not?
Choices:
A) The heal-issue skip runs first and is unchanged. Base-keying applies only when it falls through, except for `failed_jobs_differ`, which keeps today's per-PR fingerprint because that failure is partly the PR's own (RECOMMENDED)
B) The heal-issue skip runs first and is unchanged. Base-keying applies to every fall-through, including `failed_jobs_differ`, which then folds into the base issue, as the issue's "Risks" section accepts
C) Base-keying runs before the heal-issue skip and replaces it whenever a base-keyed triage issue is open
Q3: Which filings does the open-issue cap (`CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_MAX_OPEN_ISSUES`, default 5) block? A supersede files a new issue and then closes the old one, so the open count doesn't grow. A base-keyed match should also never be treated as a supersede, because every new PR has a different head.
Choices:
A) The cap applies to every new filing in normal mode. It does not apply in historical mode or to a supersede replacement, and base-keyed matches skip supersede entirely (RECOMMENDED)
B) The cap applies to every new filing in normal mode, supersede replacements included. Historical mode is exempt and base-keyed matches skip supersede
C) The cap applies to every filing, historical mode and supersede included
